Predicted effects of attention commands in A are highly specific: giving a command for a particular location almost guarantees that location will be selected next, so attention can be reliably steered to any of the four objects.

View B represents a red circular object at left, a yellow square at upper, a blue triangle at right, and a greenish cross at lower (currently the attended item). The right object is relatively accessible even though it is not currently selected; the upper and left objects are moderately accessible. Predicted effects of attention commands in B show little control: most commands drive selection toward the left location, so attempting to redirect attention generally results in the left object being selected next.
